levels.name: Benny, 22, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of hiding your screen on public transport. Level 1. Minus 40 Euro on the account, and the coconut-type screams it out loud in the packed commuter carriage while every single passenger stares directly at my glowing display with cold, merciless eyes. I am Benny, a desperate 22-year-old broccoli guy fighting for my life as an intern at a ruthless downtown tech firm, clutching my cracked smartphone on the 7:45 AM subway with my stomach in absolute knots and my hands shaking uncontrollably. You are reading job applications on company time while your bank account shows negative forty dollars? Look at his screen, everyone! Negative forty dollars! My cheeks burn bright green as I desperately try to shield the tiny display with my trembling leafy fingers, praying the train doors open before I burst into absolute tears. You will never survive in this city with that kind of exposure. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Chloe, 26, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of hiding your screen on public transport. Level 2. Level 2 offers absolute zero protection, and the arrogant, unbearable avocado-barista across the counter struts around like she owns the entire establishment while aggressively mocking every single customer. I am Chloe, a 26-year-old avocado woman working the grueling morning rush at a bustling, overheated Manhattan café, trying desperately to keep my sanity intact. This arrogant barista thinks she can humiliate me by broadcasting my most private text messages to the entire room, laughing in my face while I struggle to pay my rent. Every fiber of my being screams with pure rage at her smug expression, and as she turns her back for a single second, I prepare the ultimate, devastating revenge that will shatter her career forever. You are broadcasting your entire pathetic life to complete strangers, and nobody is going to save you from this public disaster. You will see how the tables turn when my secret corporate transfer hits my account in the next few seconds. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Mia, 24, Designer
levels.story: The 8 levels of hiding your screen on public transport. Level 3. Level 3 plunges the viewer into pure, unadulterated rage as the unbearable strawberry-designer watches her hard-earned, months-long creative work get maliciously destroyed by an envious rival before her very eyes. I am Mia, a 24-year-old strawberry woman heading to a high-stakes client pitch, carrying a tablet filled with exclusive designs that represent my entire future. Without any warning, a ruthless competitor steps forward, snatches my device, and deliberately deletes my master files while laughing maniacally for the entire bus to hear. You call these amateur sketches professional design work? Honestly, the color palette looks like trash, and nobody would ever pay for this garbage. I pull the broken device against my chest, my heart pounding like a furious drum as passengers snicker at my utter humiliation and helplessness. Real designers don't display their drafts where everyone can laugh at them, but they certainly know how to strike back when pushed too far. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Leo, 29, Accountant
levels.story: The 8 levels of hiding your screen on public transport. Level 4. Level 4 delivers a massive blow at 52 percent screen privacy, where ruthless corporate spies stop at nothing to ruin an honest man's career on the morning commute. I am Leo, a 29-year-old orange man reviewing sensitive corporate tax documents on my laptop inside a speeding commuter train. Suddenly, an aggressive pineapple character leans over my shoulder, shoving a smartphone directly into my personal space to record my confidential spreadsheets without my consent. You are hiding corporate offshore accounts on public transit? Let me see those numbers right now or face the consequences! I angle my laptop sharply against the window, my whole body trembling with white-hot rage, as my confidential data is captured on camera. I am sending this footage straight to the financial authorities right this second to destroy you. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Verena, 31, Auditor
levels.story: The 8 levels of hiding your screen on public transport. Level 5. Level 5 at 68 percent privacy brings a sickening wave of injustice as a bitter, ice-cold lemon auditor suffers a public humiliation designed to make the viewer's blood boil to 180 degrees. I am Verena, a 31-year-old lemon woman working diligently on my encrypted audit tablet inside a luxury downtown lounge, completely focused on exposing corporate fraud. Without warning, a nosy, arrogant barista struts over and deliberately spills scalding hot coffee across my pristine desk, forcing me into a panic while she loudly accuses me of corporate bankruptcy and financial ruin. You think those fake numbers will protect your failing firm from total bankruptcy? Everyone look at the corrupt auditor trying to hide her debt! My sour yellow skin tightens with pure, unmitigated fury as cruel laughter echoes through the lounge. Hiding your numbers doesn't mean the debt isn't real, but my revenge will hit even harder. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Marcus, 35, Executive
levels.story: The 8 levels of hiding your screen on public transport. Level 6. Level 6 hits with an arrogant swagger at 94.2 percent privacy, featuring an insufferable coconut-executive who treats everyone around him like absolute garbage and dares the audience to anticipate his downfall. I am Marcus, a 35-year-old coconut man riding in absolute luxury in the first-class express carriage, looking down on the pathetic peasants who cannot afford true encryption. A foolish strawberry designer dares to lean across the aisle, sneering at my private documents and trying to pry into my multi-million dollar corporate mergers. You can add privacy filters all you want, you arrogant shell of a man, but I know your company is merging and collapsing from the inside out! A merger? In this sector? Not that a peasant like you could ever comprehend it. I snap my magnetic privacy screen into place with a sharp, mocking click right in her face. Curiosity killed the strawberry, and corporate espionage pays for the bail. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Zane, 38, Security Chief
levels.story: The 8 levels of hiding your screen on public transport. Level 7. Level 7 is constructed as an absolute, inescapable dead end inside airport security where power-tripping guards and desperate trespassers collide in total chaos. I am Zane, a 38-year-old dragon fruit man managing critical national infrastructure, standing in an unyielding TSA checkpoint line with my military-grade encrypted terminal. Suddenly, an aggressive security officer blocks my path, falsely accusing me of smuggling illegal master encryption keys and demanding to search my personal belongings on the spot. You are carrying the master encryption keys for the entire transit grid in your backpack without authorization? Step back from that bag immediately or face immediate arrest! I slide my terminal into a heavy titanium briefcase with a resounding thud as armed security agents swarm around me. Some doors are locked for an absolute reason, and she just knocked on the deadliest one in the city. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: Orson, 42, System Architect
levels.story: The 8 levels of hiding your screen on public transport. Level 8. Level 8 closes the grand circle of revenge and privacy with an unforgettable, mind-bending finale that cements a legendary catchphrase in the viewer's memory forever. I am Orson, a 42-year-old watermelon man sitting at the absolute pinnacle of the central transit tower, watching all eight levels of chaos and vengeance unfold simultaneously across Citrus City. You didn't just build the transit screens... you programmed every single judgment and every single hidden number right into our foreheads. Every single glowing display in this entire metropolis is connected to this exact master desk! I sip my black coffee slowly, my watermelon core remaining as calm as solid stone while the city lights flicker in perfect synchronization below. The numbers on our foreheads were never meant to divide us—they were just reflections of what we chose to hide. Das siehst du in Level 8.
